explanation: Hero of Alexandria described a temple machine that released holy water when a coin dropped in. Spectacles appeared in Italy about 1,200 years later, in the late 1200s.

claims.text: Hero of Alexandria described a coin-operated machine that dispensed holy water in the 1st century AD.
Spectacles were first made in Italy in the late 13th century, around the 1280s.
Hero's machine released a measure of holy water when a coin was dropped into it.
Spectacles appeared about 1,200 years after Hero's coin-operated machine.

issues.note: Which came first? mixes a described machine (Hero, no surviving device) with made spectacles, and the measure field (date first described or made) is not shipped to players. A literal reader can say a coin-operated vending machine was first made in the 1800s. The explanation says described, so it is honest, but the labels could say Hero's coin-operated holy-water dispenser to make the documented event plain.
